Thanks for that. I wondered whether the effect you describe is driven by the treatment at all, or whether it might just be the natural course of the disease.
Sorry, I did not catch the second part. Could you say it again, a little more slowly?
Of course. Is it the treatment, or is it just the disease getting better on its own?
In other words, you are asking about the control group.
Exactly that.
Good. I might have misunderstood earlier, so let me be clear: we do have a control group, but it is small.
How small?
Twenty-two patients. So I would rather say the effect is probable than proven, and that is why we are extending the follow-up.
That is a fair answer. Thank you.

Right, so, thanks for that, really interesting, and I suppose what I wanted to ask, and do stop me if I have got this wrong, is whether the effect you are describing is actually driven by the treatment at all, or whether it might just be the natural course of the disease, because in our hands, and we have looked at something quite similar, the difference tends to disappear at about eighteen months, which is roughly where your follow-up ends, so I wonder if you would have seen the same thing had you carried on a bit longer. Sorry, that was a very long question.

Excuse me. I want to ask about your control group. In our centre, we had the same problem two years ago, and we solved it in a way that maybe is useful for you. We did not compare with healthy people. We compared with patients from the same clinic who did not receive the treatment, because they arrived later. It is not perfect, of course, but it removes the difference between the hospitals. If you like, I can send you the paper. It is in a small journal and I think it is not well known outside my country, but the method is simple and you could use it directly.
